title: CEMRACS 2026
description: A research project focused on generating high-temporal-resolution climate and energy data from coarse climate model outputs using stochastic diffusion processes.
longDescription: Climate model outputs such as temperature and wind speed are generally available at daily temporal resolution, while applications such as wind-generation forecasting, electricity-system analysis, and energy-price simulation often require hourly data. This project proposes modeling the variable of interest with a stochastic differential equation and developing methods to estimate its drift and volatility parameters. It also aims to simulate higher-resolution trajectories conditional on observed daily minimum, maximum, and average values.
objectives: Estimate the drift and volatility functions of the diffusion process
Generate hourly simulations from daily climate-model observations
Condition simulations on observed daily minimum, maximum, and average values
Support climate-impact and energy-market scenario analysis
Potentially extend the method to multidimensional processes
